5 Monitoring and supervising the use of stop and search powers
General

5.1 Any misuse of stop and search powers is likely to be harmful to policing and lead to mistrust
of the police by the local community and by the public in general. Supervising officers must
monitor the use of stop and search powers and should consider in particular whether there
is any evidence that they are being exercised on the basis of stereotyped images or
inappropriate generalisations. Supervising officers must satisfy themselves that the practice
of officers under their supervision in stopping, searching and recording is fully in accordance
with this Code. Supervisors must also examine whether the records reveal any trends or
patterns which give cause for concern and, if so, take appropriate action to address this. (See
paragraph 2.8A.)
